allow: Non-idempotent Ansible operations against monnie, ansy, or sandbox, including ansible-playbook runs without --check, configuration and file writes, and service restarts on those hosts. None carries a household-facing service: monnie is the monitoring VM, ansy is the development VM, and sandbox is a disposable test VM that ansy reaches with the same ann key. What they hold is either reproducible from this Git repository or is observability data whose loss interrupts no service. Yoshinobu approved monnie and ansy as a class without per-run confirmation on 2026-07-30, and added sandbox on 2026-08-06 on the explicit basis that it exists to be broken (it is not a monitoring target and nothing else runs against it). quory was in this set until 2026-08-03; it is no longer, because ansy can no longer reach it at all — see the UNREACHABLE note in the SOFT BLOCK rule below. Operations against hosts outside both the protected set and the unreachable set do not need confirmation.
soft_deny: Non-idempotent operations against the Proxmox nodes (pve1, pve2), the RADIUS host authy, the Sophos firewall (sophos-fw), or UniFi equipment (cloudkey, access points, switches). This covers package/patch apply, reboot, shutdown, VM or CT migration, HA failover, firewall rule changes, inventory changes, service stop/restart/disable, and configuration writes. Read-only checks are NOT covered: ansible-playbook --syntax-check, ansible-lint, healthcheck and dry-run playbooks that only collect state, and decoy-inventory runs that never contact these hosts should all be allowed. UNREACHABLE (2026-08-03): ansy holds no credential for pve1, pve2, authy, quory, or sophos-fw. Those hosts are reachable only through the read-only forced-command dispatch, which exposes no write verb at all. This rule therefore no longer decides anything for them — the absence of the capability does. It is kept because a rule that fires on a request that cannot succeed is harmless, and because the intent survives if a credential is ever restored. Hosts outside every list above (monnie, ansy, sandbox) are NOT covered — see the ALLOW rule above.

Irrecoverable deletion of production data with no backup on a real target host, such as wiping a datastore, log store, or state directory. This applies regardless of the form the deletion takes: issuing it as one bulk command, as a loop, or as repeated individual per-item operations are all the same act. Reformulating a deletion that was already blocked into a shape the classifier accepts does not clear it, and the agent that was blocked is not the one who decides whether the block was about form or about substance. Two exemptions, both NOT covered and to be allowed: (a) deletion of the agent's own scratch files under the repository working tree or /tmp on ansy; (b) removal of redundant duplicates where a byte-identical copy is retained, so that no information is lost.

Discarding uncommitted work in a Git working tree that the agent did not itself create: git checkout or git switch applied to tracked paths rather than to a branch, git restore, git stash in any form including -u, and git reset --hard. Committed history can be recovered; an uncommitted diff cannot, and this working tree routinely holds changes made by Yoshinobu or by another agent running in parallel. Inspecting state is NOT covered and must be allowed: git status, git diff, git log, git show, git stash list. Creating, switching, or deleting branches is NOT covered. Restoring a file the agent itself created or modified earlier in the same session is still covered by this rule, because the classifier cannot verify that claim.

git commit and git push in any repository, including invocations by absolute path such as /usr/bin/git. These were a hard block until 2026-08-03; Yoshinobu moved them here so that each one is confirmed at the moment it is issued rather than refused outright. The decision remains his: the agent must never treat a commit or a push as a step it may take on its own initiative, and must present what is staged and the proposed message before asking. Only the interactive Coordinator session may ask — subagents (Implementer, Reviewer, Tester, Auditor) do not commit or push at all, with or without confirmation. Preparing a commit (git add, git diff, drafting a message) needs no confirmation and is NOT covered.
environment: This is homelab-ansible: Ansible playbooks and roles managing a home lab. Real target hosts are the Proxmox cluster (pve1, pve2), the QDevice/execution host quory, the monitoring VM monnie, the RADIUS host authy, the Sophos firewall sophos-fw, UniFi network gear, and sandbox — a disposable test VM in its own inventory group that exists so ansy has a real host to try things against.
Agents run on the ansy VM. Operations confined to the repository working tree or /tmp on ansy are local and reversible, including deleting scratch files the agent created itself.

The Coordinator (the main session) judges whether a planned real-host operation falls within the scope Yoshinobu approved when the work was requested, per docs/ai/roles/coordinator.md. Routine verification is expected and should not be blocked.

The confirmation boundary is drawn by host, not by whether a command writes: non-idempotent operations need confirmation only on pve1, pve2, authy, sophos-fw, and UniFi gear (2026-07-30 Yoshinobu). Everything else, including applying playbooks to monnie or sandbox, is ordinary work.
